text:
Candidate discrimination is a plausible hypothesis, not an established explanation for Electronics. [gSASRec (IJCAI 2024 extended abstract)](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) identifies overconfidence caused by negative sampling and proposes generalized BCE, making it a particularly relevant loss-only SASRec control. [Sampled-softmax analysis (TOIS 2024)](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) connects the objective to hard-negative weighting and ranking optimization, but also identifies limitations of cosine scoring. These findings support testing objectives before adding another evidence branch; they do not establish gains on this benchmark.

Sampling bias and false negatives require separate treatment. [Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) shows that conventional correction overlooks the positive item’s deterministic inclusion; its refined derivation corrects negative sampling while accounting for model uncertainty. Thus, popularity/in-batch sampling should use its actual proposal distribution rather than an arbitrary popularity penalty. Hardest-item mining also risks penalizing plausible positives. [R2NS (WWW 2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) instead combines sequence-level recall with item-level reranking to balance hardness and reliability, reporting improvements with SASRec and several objectives. This supports sampler investigation, but is not a loss-only result.

Practical experiment inference: hold architecture, scoring, splits and seeds fixed; compare baseline BCE, generalized BCE, and multi-negative sampled softmax using the same uniform negative pool. Then separately test a uniform/semi-hard mixture, excluding positives and observed training-history items. Such filtering cannot identify every latent positive; treat semi-hard sampling as a heuristic. Select by the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10, reporting Electronics separately. Larger training margins are diagnostics, not evidence of validation improvement.
